steps.tx: Thickening of the pylorus muscle blocking stomach emptying in young infants is **congenital hypertrophic pyloric stenosis**. It typically appears at two to eight weeks with forceful non bilious vomiting after feeds. The hungry baby loses weight and becomes dehydrated with low chloride and potassium.
steps.say: Hypertrophic pyloric stenosis blocks stomach emptying at two to eight weeks with forceful non bilious vomiting.

steps.tx: The firm pylorus felt in the right upper abdomen during a test feed is the **olive mass**. Feeling it confirms the diagnosis clinically, though ultrasound is now usual. The thickened muscle measures over four millimetres on ultrasound criteria. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: The olive mass felt during a test feed confirms pyloric stenosis clinically.

steps.tx: Splitting the thickened pylorus muscle lengthwise without cutting mucosa is **Ramstedt pyloromyotomy**. Fluids and salts are corrected before surgery, never rushed as an emergency operation. Feeding usually resumes within hours of the procedure. Correlating this finding with imaging and laboratory results prevents both delayed treatment and unnecessary intervention in most patients.
steps.say: Ramstedt pyloromyotomy splits the thickened muscle after fluids and salts are corrected first.

steps.tx: Telescoping of one bowel segment into the next is **intussusception**. It peaks between six months and two years, causing colicky pain, vomiting and a sausage shaped abdominal mass. Most cases have no lead point in this age group. Early recognition matters because timely treatment gives clearly better outcomes than waiting for complications to develop first.
steps.say: Intussusception telescopes bowel in infants, causing colicky pain and a sausage shaped mass.

steps.tx: Ultrasound shows concentric bowel rings described as the **target sign**. This confirms intussusception quickly without radiation. Air or fluid enema under imaging guidance is then attempted for reduction. Students should connect this fact with the presenting symptoms, since examination questions usually test that clinical link directly.
steps.say: The target sign on ultrasound confirms intussusception before guided enema reduction.

steps.tx: Correcting dehydration and salt loss before pyloromyotomy follows the rule of **resuscitation first**. The metabolic alkalosis from vomiting hydrochloric acid must settle. Operating on a depleted baby risks anaesthetic complications. Documenting this finding clearly in the notes guides the next clinician and supports safe, well planned further management.
steps.say: Resuscitation first corrects alkalosis before pyloromyotomy because depleted babies risk anaesthetic complications.

steps.tx: First born boys are affected most often in pyloric stenosis, a pattern of **male predominance**. Family history also increases risk in siblings. Macrolide antibiotics in early life are a recognised association. When this picture is seen in practice, urgent senior review is wise whenever there is any doubt about severity.
steps.say: Pyloric stenosis favours first born boys and runs in families.

steps.tx: Projectile vomiting that is never green separates pyloric stenosis from **bilious obstruction**. Bile stained vomiting in an infant means obstruction beyond the duodenum and needs urgent surgical assessment. Colour of vomit is therefore a key history point. Understanding this mechanism explains the symptoms, the investigation findings and the logic behind each step of treatment given.
steps.say: Non bilious vomiting fits pyloric stenosis, while green vomiting means urgent surgical obstruction.

steps.tx: After successful pyloromyotomy, vomiting may persist briefly from stomach atony called **postoperative settling**. It resolves within a day or two without further surgery. Persistent vomiting beyond that needs re-evaluation for incomplete myotomy. This distinction changes management, so it should be settled early rather than after empirical treatment has already begun.
steps.say: Brief vomiting after pyloromyotomy settles in days, while persistence needs re-evaluation.
